description:
The short "Summary" spreadsheet download of Sales By Representative leaves out four of the columns the report shows on screen: # Invoices, # Customers, Hrs Worked and Hrs Invoiced. It also adds a Totals row that this download is not supposed to have.

The figures are not missing from the report itself — only from the downloaded file.
steps: Open Reports, then Sales By Representative.
Leave every control at its default: date range This Month, Product Type Parts & Service, All Statuses, All locations.
Read the column headings on screen and note that # Invoices, # Customers, Hrs Worked and Hrs Invoiced are among them.
Open the three-dot menu and choose the Summary CSV download.
Open the downloaded file in a plain text editor, not a spreadsheet application, so the real first line is visible.
Compare its heading row with what was read in step 3, then scroll to the bottom of the file and look for a Totals row.
current:
The Summary spreadsheet has ten columns, and this exact heading row read straight out of the file:

Representative,Location,"Inv. Hrs","Labor Invoiced","Labor Margin","Parts Invoiced","Parts Margin",Margin,"Margin %",Subtotal

# Invoices, # Customers, Hrs Worked and Hrs Invoiced are not in it. The file also ends with a Totals row.

The longer Expanded spreadsheet of the same report does contain Hrs Worked and Hrs Invoiced, so the figures reach the download code.
expected: The Summary spreadsheet carries the same columns the Summary view shows on screen, including # Invoices, # Customers, Hrs Worked and Hrs Invoiced, and it has no Totals row.
source: Summary CSV — file sales-by-representative-summary.csv, UTF-8 BOM, one header row + one row per rep in the current filtered view, in the currently-active order (S14-R2a). Headers, in order: Representative, # Invoices, # Customers, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Inv. Hrs, Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin, Margin, Margin %, Subtotal.
Chris Ward confirmed the same thing in our questions spreadsheet
That answer is from the tab "The product vs your write-up", row 9, on 5 August 2026. It agrees with the requirement above; nothing is being overridden.
